title: Princeton deep RL controller steers DIII-D plasmas clear of tearing instability; only two of the controlled shots disrupt
summary: An RL controller trained on a tearing-likelihood model kept DIII-D plasmas below the instability threshold; before RL control all but one shot disrupted, after it only two did (Nature, 21 Feb 2024).
account: Seo et al. (Nature, published 21 February 2024), from Princeton University, the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory and partners, trained a reinforcement-learning controller in an environment built from a multimodal dynamic model that estimates the likelihood of future tearing instability, the leading cause of disruptions. Deployed on DIII-D, the largest magnetic fusion facility in the United States, located at General Atomics in San Diego, the controller adjusted total beam power and plasma triangularity to keep the estimated tearability under a threshold while maintaining H-mode performance, even at low safety factor and low torque. In the experimental session, discharges up to 193276 either had no RL control or tore before control started; of the controlled discharges from 193277, only two (193277 and 193282) were disrupted, whereas before RL control all shots except one were disrupted, and average time-integrated normalised beta rose. Princeton Engineering's release (21 February 2024) says the model could forecast tearing mode instabilities up to 300 milliseconds in advance. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor logged the result as a positive outcome (record 2024-02-24-7d77). The experiment dates are not given; the date used is the paper's publication date.
purpose: The controller was built to avoid tearing instability while maintaining high-pressure plasma in DIII-D; the avoided disruptions were its intended use.
system: Deep reinforcement learning tearing-avoidance controller with a DNN tearability predictor (Keras model converted to real-time C)
developer: Princeton University / Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (Kolemen group), with Chung-Ang University
deployer: DIII-D National Fusion Facility, General Atomics
taxonomy_note: A capability demonstration on a DOE user facility; disruption counts are reported for one experimental session, not routine operation. Classed as benefit created for the identified controlled discharges.

ratings.reason: The DIII-D session obtained plasmas tracking a stable path with fewer disruptions and higher time-integrated beta; the paper calls it a path toward ITER-relevant scenarios.
No outcome beyond fusion research is documented.

ai_role.statement: The RL controller set the high-level actuator commands that the plasma control system executed, so the disruption outcomes in the controlled shots are attributable to it, with the caveats that the comparison is within one session and the paper is authored by the system's developers; independent evaluation is the journal's peer review and the OECD AIM registry entry.
